findings.location: vectors T49 and stores.splits; scripts/topology_coordination.py _held_out (held_digests); README A3 ('MAS-RA-002's store-relative rule')
findings.finding: MAS-RA-002's held-out rule has two routes, and the vectors leave one property of the content-digest route unpinned. The rule is 'by content digest in any suite, by task ID in the same suite'. Round 4 pins the ID route's suite boundary: N03 is now killed by T01/T02 through the new other-suite declaration. But the content-digest route is exercised only within one suite. T49's record alt-a (split-alt, suite ..000001) is held out by split-001, split-late and split-one, all of the same suite. A mutant that restricts the digest route to the record's own suite (R13) passes every vector. The model is right. In probe P03, a valid declaration of another suite that holds out T02's first DEVELOPMENT task by digest only (another task ID) makes dev-low NOT_ELIGIBLE. Under R13 the same record stays eligible (3/10), so it would unlock SELF_ORGANIZING. That cross-suite digest route is what stops a held-out task renamed into another suite from being used as selection input (Q-MAS2-C (a), the subject of round 1's M4R1-2).
findings.requiredChange: Add a vector in which only a declaration of another suite holds out a record's DEVELOPMENT task by content digest (with a different task ID), and the record is refused SELECTION. For example, move T49's holding declaration to another suite, or add a T52 on such a declaration.

findings.finding: The no-surrogate part of the scope-text rule is not exercised for Python-object inputs. Mutant R16 (surrogates allowed) passes every vector. Text inputs are unaffected, because parse() already refuses any lone surrogate as SHAPE (text X03), and schema and model agree (round-3 probe P05).
findings.requiredChange: Optional: a SHAPE vector with a lone surrogate in tenantId or in a scope member.

findings.finding: Two different valid declarations share the splitId 'split-other-suite': the original one (suite ..000004, o1-o3 / o9) and the new one (suite ..e2d400, o1 / t1). MAS-RA-002 does not require unique split ids, and nothing depends on it, but the README text 'plus one of another suite' is easier to follow with a distinct id.
